original_question: If delta(Gamma) denotes the smoothability defect of a finite scheme Gamma, is it true that for every epsilon > 0, the ratio delta(Gamma^{times n}) / (deg Gamma)^{n(1+epsilon)} tends to 0 as n tends to infinity?
target_in_paper: Problem XXXVI in §2.9 ("Smoothability"), with the notation and definition of δ(Γ) supplied by Problem XXXV and the global conventions supplied by §1.3. This paper is a problem list, so the nearest official formulation is this numbered problem, not an introductory conjecture/proposition/theorem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper: it fixes a finite scheme Γ, uses the smoothability defect δ(Γ), asks about the asymptotic behavior of δ(Γ^{× n}), normalizes by (deg Γ)^{n(1+ε)}, quantifies over every ε>0, and asks whether the limit is 0. That is essentially Problem XXXVI verbatim. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
missing_details: The paper works throughout over an algebraically closed field k, so the question should say explicitly that Γ is a finite k-scheme. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
The notation deg Γ means the degree/length of the finite scheme Γ, not the cardinality of its support. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
To be stand-alone, δ(Γ) must be defined from Problem XXXV: it is the minimal possible difference deg Γ′−deg Γ where Γ ⊆ Γ′ and Γ′ is finite smoothable. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.08777))

The notation Γ^{× n} should be spelled out as the n-fold self-product Γ×_k⋯×_kΓ over the ground field; this is implicit in the paper’s notation Γ^{× n}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
It should be explicit that Γ is fixed and n ranges over positive integers with n→∞. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.08777))

If full stand-alone readability is desired, retain the paper’s adjective 'smoothable' in the definition of δ(Γ) rather than assuming the reader already knows it from the surrounding section. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
refined_question:
Let k be an algebraically closed field, let Γ be a finite k-scheme, and let δ(Γ) denote its smoothability defect, i.e. the minimum of deg Γ′−deg Γ over all finite smoothable k-schemes Γ′ such that Γ ⊆ Γ′. Is it true that for every ε>0, if Γ^{× n}:=Γ×_k⋯×_kΓ denotes the n-fold self-product of Γ, then
lim_{n→∞} δ(Γ^{× n})/(deg Γ)^{n(1+ε)} = 0?
Here deg Γ denotes the degree (length) of Γ. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
justification: The draft is targeting Problem XXXVI almost exactly. Problem XXXV, immediately before it, introduces the smoothability defect δ(Γ), and §1.3 fixes the ambient conventions needed to make the problem stand alone: all schemes are over an algebraically closed field k, and degree means length for finite schemes. The surrounding discussion after Problem XXXVI explains that the author intends this precise asymptotic vanishing statement because of its connection with Strassen-type questions and the matrix multiplication exponent, so the refined version should stay narrowly at that limit statement and not broaden to neighboring smoothability-growth questions. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
